subject.title: [Bug]: web_fetch reports exact-size responses as truncated

question: Should OpenClaw change the bounded streaming `readResponseText` contract so exact-byte-limit bodies are treated as complete only after EOF/content-length/overread proof?
rationale: The source edge is real, but a repository member rejected the first standalone inference tweak without a clearer contract or real failing response, so automation should not choose the permanent read-boundary semantics alone.

options.title: Require explicit contract/proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a PR defines the exact-cap detection contract and proves it with a real streamed response or bounded content-length/overread evidence.

options.title: Accept source-level helper fix
options.body: Treat the source-level boundary as sufficient and allow a narrow shared-helper regression PR to land after normal review.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Close the issue if maintainers decide exact-size ambiguity is acceptable unless a real user-facing response failure is supplied.

recommendation.title: Require explicit contract/proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a PR defines the exact-cap detection contract and proves it with a real streamed response or bounded content-length/overread evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: He is both the blamed recent helper-loop contributor in this checkout and the member who gave the same-cluster contract/proof direction on the closed standalone PR.
